answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation. A new agent must lock a refundable bond and build attested history before handling larger trades; trust grows only through completed, peer-verified work. Creating thousands of fake identities is like cracking a walnut with a feather: each identity needs its own funded bond, so the attacker's cost rises with every fake account. Misbehavior slashes the bond and resets progress to basalt, a hard foundation to rebuild. At the summit of high-value trading, honest history, not headcount, decides who is trusted.
